acceptance: ConnectorToolkitSchema gains a required `custody: ConnectorCustodySchema` field with TSDoc explaining that the client's custody chip reads it and must never infer custody.

registry.listToolkits() sets `custody` from the yielding provider's getCapabilities().custody; the dedupe-by-slug keeps the higher-precedence stance using the SAME managed > self-host > external order routing.ts already documents (extract the shared precedence constant rather than duplicating the map).
Every provider path that returns toolkits (composio, nango, raw-mcp, test-mode, FakeConnectorProvider in @dorkos/test-utils) satisfies the widened schema; connectorConformance still passes unchanged.
No client code is touched in this task; the field is additive and the server always populates it.

tasks.title: Curated service catalog + custody-chip derivation, as pure tested data and functions
acceptance: service-catalog.ts exports SERVICE_CATALOG: one entry per known service with { slug, displayName, capabilityLine, facet?, route: 'engine' | 'relay', mark? }; 12-14 entries sized per spec OQ4, every capabilityLine one plain sentence naming what an agent can do, no hype, no counts, no pricing (writing-for-humans).
Slack's entry is route: 'relay' and no entry anywhere claims a direct route (founder decision 6).

custody-chip.ts exports a pure `custodyChipFor(entry, toolkits)` whose ONLY custody input is ConnectorToolkit.custody from the server (spec D4). There is no client-side direct-slug list and no inference from 'which provider is configured'.

The derivation is a switch over ConnectorCustody with a `never`-typed fallthrough guard mirroring assertUnreachableCustody (apps/server/src/services/connectors/custody-disclosure.ts:114), so widening the enum is a compile error here until the chip handles it.

It handles today's three members: 'managed' -> `via Composio`, 'self-host' -> `Self-hosted`, 'external' -> `Direct` (sentence: connects straight to the service, no other company holds this sign-in). The 'direct' branch and its own sentence ('the key stays on your machine') are written now and become reachable when specs/direct-connect D1.5 adds the enum member; zero `direct` toolkits is the normal tested state until then.

A catalog entry with route: 'relay' resolves to `DorkOS adapter` regardless of toolkits; a service no live toolkit lists resolves to `Needs setup`, and that label contains NO vendor name — asserted, because it is the claim that must never be wrong.
TSDoc on every export; barrel exports only.
tasks.testPlan: pnpm vitest run apps/client/src/layers/features/connections/__tests__/custody-chip.test.ts — one case per handled custody value ('managed', 'self-host', 'external'), plus: a relay-routed entry ignores toolkits; a slug with no toolkit yields Needs setup whose label contains neither 'Composio' nor 'Nango'; a cast-in 'direct' value returns the Direct chip with the key-stays-on-your-machine sentence (pins the branch before the enum widens). Add a type-level check that removing a switch arm fails typecheck (pnpm --filter @dorkos/client typecheck) — that is the real regression gate. No DOM needed.

tasks.title: One curl before any import code: does a Composio project key list the project's accounts?
acceptance: Run, with the founder's real project API key (the one created for the #617 retest), a single GET against Composio's v3.1 connected-accounts endpoint with NO user_ids filter, and record the verbatim status and body shape in the PR description (key redacted, never committed).

Answer recorded as one of two outcomes, in the spec's OQ2 entry: YES (the project's accounts come back) -> R2.2 and R2.3 proceed exactly as specced; NO (403/scope refusal or an empty list that is provably filtered) -> R2.2 and R2.3 SHRINK to the connect-again-through-DorkOS path alone: no listImportableAccounts, no importable route, no adopt route, no import panel, and Advanced instead carries the one honest line from OQ2.
Also record what user_id the pre-existing dashboard accounts carry, because it decides OQ3 (whether an adopted account's tools can resolve).
No production code changes in this task. If the outcome is NO, edit OQ2 to say so and stop — do not invent a scope, an org key, or a second credential.
tasks.testPlan: Manual, one command, at EXECUTE start. No test suite. The deliverable is the recorded answer plus the scope decision for R2.2/R2.3, written into 02-specification.md OQ2 so the next agent inherits the fact rather than the assumption.

tasks.title: Server: list the accounts already in the aggregator, and adopt one honestly
acceptance: ConnectorProvider gains OPTIONAL listImportableAccounts?(): Promise<ConnectedAccount[]>; connectorConformance is unchanged and raw-MCP implements nothing.

Composio implements it by listing connected accounts WITHOUT the user_ids filter. R2.0 has already answered whether that works; if R2.0 came back NO, this task and R2.3 are cancelled in favour of the connect-again-only path and the honest Advanced line (spec OQ2).

GET /api/connectors/accounts/importable returns { accounts: PublicConnectedAccount[], warnings } with any id already bound in connected_accounts filtered out, aggregating per provider and degrading to warnings[] exactly like the other aggregate reads (ADR-0310).

POST /api/connectors/accounts/:accountId/adopt records the binding via registry.recordConnect, then probes provider.toolServerForAccount and returns { account, toolsReachable, error? }; a probe failure is reported, never thrown; an unknown id is 404.

Transport gains getImportableConnectorAccounts() and adoptConnectorAccount(accountId), implemented in HttpTransport and honestly in DirectTransport; createMockTransport in @dorkos/test-utils covers both.
test-mode implements listImportableAccounts with scripted rows so e2e can drive the flow; OpenAPI regenerated.
No secret, credential reference, or vendor handle beyond the existing opaque id crosses either response.

tasks.title: Curated try-it prompts, selected by the role recommender that already ships
acceptance: TRY_IT_PROMPTS covers the eight slugs CONNECTOR_DISPLAY_NAMES already names, each with a default prompt and optional byRole overrides keyed by CanonRoleId; every prompt is a sentence a person would actually type.

pickTryItPrompt(slug, roles) uses recommendForRoles(roles) to find the role that recommended this service and prefers its byRole prompt, falling back to the default; an unknown slug returns undefined so the affordance is simply absent.
The function is pure and deterministic; no I/O, no randomness.
TSDoc explains that recommendForRoles is the role signal (founder decision 5) and that prompts are curated, never generated.

tasks.title: One tap from connected to working: attach, navigate, prefill, and one restrained arrival
acceptance: startTryItNow mints a UUID, calls attachSessionConnector(sessionId, accountId), and only then navigates to /session with { session, prompt }; a failed attach shows the verbatim error in a role=alert and does NOT navigate.

The attach-before-the-session-exists behavior is pinned as a CONTRACT, not left as an accident: a new case in apps/server/src/routes/__tests__/session-connectors.test.ts attaches a known account to a session id that has never been created and asserts 200 with the disclosure, carrying a comment that names try-it-now (specs/connections-redesign §7) as the dependent so anyone adding session-id validation reads why first. The hole is deliberately NOT closed.
The connect dialog's connected step and an adopted import row both offer `Try it now` with the exact prompt visible above it; the composer is prefilled and nothing is auto-sent.
The affordance is absent when pickTryItPrompt returns undefined.

The newly connected account row animates once (160ms fade and rise, motion, tokens only); under prefers-reduced-motion there is no motion and the row carries a `Just connected` chip until the next interaction, so feedback is never simply dropped.
The animation is suppressed while any provider-rejected notice is on screen — nothing celebrates during an incident.
